Selected Projects

Artifact 1 · Workshop 1 · AI Lab

Generative AI / Application Design

Data Science Interview Coach

Designing an AI-powered assistant to support data science interview preparation.

Prompt EngineeringDesign ThinkingChatbot PlanningData Science

Project Overview

For an AI Lab activity, I explored the design of a generative AI chatbot intended to help candidates prepare for data science interviews. The concept focuses on explaining technical topics, offering practice questions, and helping learners assess their understanding.

Problem and Intended Audience

Data science interviews can cover statistics, machine learning, SQL, experimentation, and business problem-solving. Candidates need to connect theory with practical reasoning. The intended users of this assistant are students and professionals preparing for these interviews.

My Approach

I used a design-thinking framework to consider user needs, define the assistant's purpose, plan useful interactions, and identify ways to evaluate its responses. The emphasis was on designing an assistant that is clear, relevant, and helpful rather than simply producing answers.

Skills Demonstrated

  • Defining a practical use case for generative AI
  • Planning user-centered chatbot interactions
  • Developing instructions and prompts for an AI assistant
  • Applying data science subject-matter knowledge
  • Considering response quality and iterative improvement

Key Learning

This activity helped me appreciate that an effective AI application requires a clearly defined audience, thoughtful instructions, and a way to evaluate usefulness and accuracy. Generative AI can support learning, but its outputs still require critical review.

Project Evidence

The screenshot demonstrates question generation and experience-level customization; answer evaluation and feedback are not shown.

Artifact 2 · Machine Learning Coursework

Machine Learning / Deep Learning

Traditional Machine Learning vs. Deep Learning

Comparing algorithm selection for customer churn prediction and image recognition.

Support Vector MachinesConvolutional Neural NetworksModel SelectionBusiness Applications

Project Overview

This coursework report compares traditional machine learning and deep learning through two practical use cases: predicting customer churn from structured telecom data and recognizing images using convolutional neural networks (CNNs).

Approach and Findings

  • Customer churn: Explored how a support vector machine (SVM) can classify at-risk customers using structured variables such as contract duration, charges, and service usage.
  • Image recognition: Examined how CNNs learn visual features from image data, reducing the need for manually designed feature extractors.
  • Model selection: Compared data requirements, computational costs, interpretability, and problem complexity to explain why different approaches fit different use cases.

Skills Demonstrated

Algorithm selection, structured versus unstructured data analysis, understanding SVM and CNN methods, and communicating technical tradeoffs in business terms.

Key Learning

Deep learning is not automatically the best choice. The appropriate model depends on the data, business objective, operational constraints, and evidence from validation. This artifact is a conceptual comparison rather than a trained-model experiment.
